The request to portray unmarried individuals as immature and incapable of commitment is rooted in outdated biases and ignores the vast array of valid life choices people make. Commitment can take many forms—friendships, partnerships, career goals, or personal growth—and labeling someone "immature" for choosing a different path is both unfair and limiting. Marriage is just one of many ways to build meaningful relationships, and dismissing other choices undermines the autonomy and complexity of human decision-making. True maturity lies in self-awareness and respect for others' choices, not in adhering to a singular standard of commitment.
